questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a basic component of a computer network?
questions.solution_en:
The basic components of a computer network include:

· Sender (the device initiating communication)

· Receiver (the device receiving communication)

· Message (the data being transmitted)

· Transmission medium (the physical path like cables or wireless signals)

· Protocols (rules governing communication)

· Network devices (routers, switches, etc.)

While power supply is necessary for the devices to operate, it's not considered a basic component of the network architecture itself.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements related to computer networks:

I. A Local Area Network (LAN) typically covers a larger geographical area than a Metropolitan Area Network (MAN).

II. A Wide Area Network (WAN) can span across countries and continents.

Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution_en:
Statement II is correct because WANs (Wide Area Networks) do span across countries and continents. Statement I is incorrect because LANs (Local Area Networks) typically cover smaller areas than MANs (Metropolitan Area Networks), not larger areas.

The typical coverage hierarchy is:

· LANs: Smallest (building, campus)

· MANs: Medium (city, metropolitan area)

· WANs: Largest (countries, continents, global)

questions.q_en: Which network topology connects each device to a central hub or switch?
questions.solution_en:
In a star topology, all devices connect to a central hub or switch, creating a star-like pattern. This provides centralized management and fault isolation.

Bus Topology:

· All devices are connected to a single cable, called a bus or backbone.

Ring Topology:

· Devices are connected in a closed loop, with each device connected to two other devices.

Mesh Topology:

· Devices are interconnected with many redundant connections between them.

questions.q_en: What is the function of a router in a computer network?
options_en: To divide network connections among multiple devices
To connect a LAN to an internet connection
To convert digital data into analog signals
To connect multiple devices on a computer network
questions.solution_en:
A router's primary function is to connect a LAN to an internet connection, allowing devices on the local network to communicate with external networks.

Routers operate at the network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model.

questions.q_en: In a Star topology, what is the primary role of the central node?
options_en: To act as a repeater, amplifying signals across the network.
To function as the main server, storing all network data.
To serve as a central connection point for all devices in the network.
To prevent unauthorized access to the network.
questions.solution_en:
In a star topology, each device connects to a central hub or switch, making the central node the focal point of communication.

While hubs can act as repeaters, this is not their primary role in a star topology. Switches, which are more common in modern star networks, don't amplify signals in the same way.

The central node in a star topology is typically a hub or a switch, not a server. Servers can be connected to the network, but they are separate entities.

While switches can provide some basic security features, dedicated firewalls or security devices are used for robust network security

questions.q_en:
Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for error detection and correction?

I. Network Layer

II. Transport Layer

III. Data-Link Layer

IV. Session Layer

V. Physical Layer
questions.solution_en:
Data-Link Layer:

· This layer is responsible for error detection and correction within a local network segment (e.g., Ethernet).

· It uses techniques like Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) to detect errors and may retransmit frames to correct them.

Transport Layer:

· This layer provides end-to-end error detection and correction between applications.

· Protocols like TCP use checksums and acknowledgments to ensure reliable data delivery, including error detection and retransmission.

questions.q_en: Which layer of the OSI model manages device addressing and tracks the location of devices on the network?
questions.solution_en:
· Network Layer:

o The network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model is primarily responsible for logical addressing (IP addresses) and routing.

o It determines the best path for data packets to travel from source to destination across different networks.

o Therefore, it manages device addressing and tracks the location of devices in a network.

· Transport Layer:

o The transport layer (Layer 4) focuses on reliable end-to-end delivery of data, including segmentation, error control, and flow control.

· Session Layer:

o The session layer (Layer 5) manages communication sessions between applications, establishing, maintaining, and terminating connections.

· Presentation Layer:

o The presentation layer (Layer 6) handles data formatting, encryption, and compression, ensuring that data is presented in a way that applications can understand.

questions.q_en: What is the main function of the TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)?
options_en: To translate domain names into IP addresses
To provide unreliable transport of data packets
To provide reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of data
questions.solution_en:
· TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures data is delivered reliably.

· It establishes a connection before transmitting data, segments the data into packets, and reassembles them in the correct order at the destination.

· It uses mechanisms like acknowledgments and retransmissions to handle errors and ensure data integrity.

questions.q_en: Which layer of the TCP/IP model is a combination of the Physical and Data Link layers of the OSI model?
questions.solution_en:
The TCP/IP model's Network Access Layer handles the functions of the OSI model's Physical and Data Link layers.

This layer is the lowest layer in the TCP/IP model.

Its primary responsibility is to handle the physical transmission of data between devices on the same network.

It essentially combines the functions of the OSI model's Physical and Data Link layers:

· Physical Layer Functions:

o Deals with the physical medium of transmission (e.g., cables, wireless signals).

o Defines electrical and physical specifications.

o Handles bit-level transmission.

· Data Link Layer Functions:

o Handles error detection and correction within a local network segment.

o Provides addressing (MAC addresses).

o Handles framing (organizing bits into frames).

o Manages access to the physical medium.

Examples:

· Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and other local area network (LAN) technologies operate at the Network Access Layer.

Further insights:

OSI Model vs. TCP/IP Model

· OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) Model:

o A conceptual framework that standardizes the functions of a telecommunication or computing system into a communication protocol.

o It has seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

· TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) Model:

o A practical model used by the Internet.

o It has four layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, and Application.

questions.q_en: Which protocol is used to find the physical address from the IP address?
questions.solution_en:
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to find the physical address (MAC address) from the IP address. It's essential for mapping network layer addresses to link layer addresses.

When a device needs to communicate with another device on the same network, it uses ARP to determine the target device's MAC address. This is necessary because data is ultimately transmitted based on MAC addresses at the Data Link Layer.

questions.q_hi:
निम्नलिखित का मिलान करें: नेटवर्क प्रोटोकॉल और उनके पोर्ट नंबर।

कॉलम A (प्रोटोकॉल)कॉलम B (पोर्ट नंबर)
A.HTTP1.22
B.HTTPS2.80
C.FTP3.443
D.SSH4.21
questions.solution_en:
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) - 80

· HTTP is the foundation of the World Wide Web. It's used for transferring web pages and other web content.

· Port 80 is the standard port for unencrypted HTTP traffic. When you type a website address into your browser (without "https://"), your browser typically connects to port 80 by default.

HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) - 443

· HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP. It encrypts the communication between your browser and the web server, protecting sensitive information like passwords and credit card numbers.

· Port 443 is the standard port for HTTPS traffic.

FTP (File Transfer Protocol) - 21

· FTP is used for transferring files between computers over a network.

· Port 21 is the control port for FTP. It's used to establish connections and send commands. Port 20 is used for the data connection in active FTP mode.

SSH (Secure Shell) - 22

· SSH is a secure protocol used for remote login and other network services. It provides encrypted communication, protecting against eavesdropping and other attacks.

· Port 22 is the standard port for SSH.

Further insights:

Understanding Port Numbers

· Purpose: Port numbers are like extensions on an IP address. They allow a single computer to run multiple network services simultaneously. When data arrives at an IP address, the port number tells the operating system which application or service should receive it.

· Range: Port numbers range from 0 to 65535.

· Well-Known Ports: Ports 0 to 1023 are "well-known" or "system" ports. They are assigned to common services and are usually reserved for system processes or services run by privileged users.

questions.q_en: What is the function of a Network Interface Card (NIC)?
options_en: It connects a computer to a network
It converts analog signals to digital signals
questions.solution_en:
A Network Interface Card connects a computer to a network by providing the hardware interface between the computer and the network medium. It operates at both the Physical and Data Link layers.

It implements the physical layer circuitry necessary for communicating with a data link layer standard, such as Ethernet or Wi-Fi. Each card represents a device and can prepare, transmit and control the flow of data on the network.

The NIC uses the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model to send signals at the physical layer, transmit data packets at the network layer and operate as an interface at the TCP/IP layer.

Some types of NICs include the following:

· Wireless. NICs that use an antenna to provide wireless reception through radio frequency waves. Wi-Fi connections use wireless NICs.

· Wired. NICs that have input jacks made for cables. Ethernet is the most popular wired LAN technology.

· USB. NICs that provide network connections through a device plugged into the USB port.

· Fiber optics. NICs used as a high-speed support system for network traffic handling on server computers. It's also possible to achieve this support by combining multiple NICs. Fiber optic NICs are typically more expensive and complex.

questions.q_en: Which transmission medium uses light pulses to transmit data?
questions.solution_en:
· Fiber-optic cables consist of thin strands of glass or plastic that transmit data as pulses of light. This allows for very high bandwidth and long-distance transmission with minimal signal loss.

· Coaxial and twisted-pair cables use electrical signals, and "Ethernet cable" refers to a type of cable that commonly uses twisted pair wiring to transmit electrical signals.

questions.q_en: What is the purpose of multiplexing in data communication?
options_en: To encrypt data for secure transmission
To combine multiple data streams over a single medium
questions.solution_en:
· Multiplexing allows multiple signals or data streams to share a common communication channel.

· This efficiently utilizes the available bandwidth, reducing the need for separate communication lines for each signal.

· It's a technique used to maximize the capacity of a transmission medium.

questions.q_en: Which type of multiplexing divides the available bandwidth into different frequency channels?
questions.solution_en:
· Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM): This technique assigns a separate frequency band to each signal or data stream. These frequency bands are separated by guard bands to prevent interference.

· Time Division Multiplexing (TDM): This divides the available time into slots, allocating a slot to each signal.

· Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM): This is used in fiber-optic communications and divides the available bandwidth into different wavelengths (colors) of light.

· Asynchronous TDM: This is a form of TDM where time slots are allocated dynamically based on demand.
